# Kavach

> Kavach turns production crashes in journal-driven services, in any language, into deterministic fixtures that AI coding agents can reproduce, fix and verify. A fix counts only when `kavach diff` prints `fixed`: the recorded failure is gone, invariants hold, earlier outputs match production, and at least 10 perturbed variants of the incident (on which the old build fails the same way) pass too. Scope is single-writer, journal-driven services; a service takes part through an SDK or by speaking two protocols directly. Pre-alpha: APIs and the format will change before 1.0.

Start with AGENTS.md. It is the loop to follow and the table of verdicts. Never edit, regenerate or delete a fixture (`*.kavach`) to make something pass, and report verdicts exactly as Kavach prints them.

## Agent guide

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): the reproduce, fix, verify loop; every verdict and what to do about it; exit codes; the MCP tools.
- [INTEGRATING.md](INTEGRATING.md): adding Kavach to a language or service with no SDK, by speaking the recorder and host protocols directly; done when the conformance suites pass.

## Docs

- [README.md](README.md): the demo (a wallet ledger that crashes on `"amount": null`), how recording, replay and verification work, and what is out of scope.
- [SPEC.md](SPEC.md): the journal and fixture format, the fix-verification rules (section 6.1), and the host and recorder protocols (sections 9 and 10).
- [BENCHMARKS.md](BENCHMARKS.md): every published number, with the command that measured it.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): DCO sign-off is required on every commit; keep pull requests small.

## Code

- [examples/ledger](examples/ledger): the demo service, in Go, with a fixture (`testdata/null-amount.kavach`), the planted bug, a correct fix (`-tags ledgerfix`) and a too-narrow one (`-tags ledgerpartialfix`).
- [bench](bench): ten planted bugs, each with a correct and a too-narrow fix, run with `go test ./bench -v`.
- [sdk](sdk): the SDKs, one per language (Go, Python, TypeScript, Rust, Java, C and C++, Julia, Ruby, PHP, Elixir, Haskell, OCaml), each with a port of the ledger demo.
- [replay](replay): the replay engine, host-protocol driver and fix verification behind the CLI.
- [cmd/kavach](cmd/kavach): the CLI (`inspect`, `replay`, `diff`, `list`) and the MCP server (`kavach mcp`).
